title: Model Shelf Fast-Track: Competitive Signal Prioritization & Diligence Runbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: produce an operational runbook that converts continuous competitive signals into a prioritized, auditable diligence workflow for adding or deprecating model flavors on the Redwood model shelf.

Scope:
- Define signal taxonomy (latency, quant-compatibility, stability, licensing risk, token cost, regional availability).
- Map signals to priority weights and escalation gates.
- Create lightweight diligence template for PM/Eng/Legal to approve model shelf changes.
- Deliver an initial pilot prioritization for 12 candidate model flavors and a recommended canary plan.

Why now: rapid emergence of model variants is increasing ops churn and procurement risk. We need a repeatable, data-driven way to decide which flavors to onboard or deprecate while preserving SLAs and unit economics.
acceptance_criteria: Signal taxonomy documented and reviewed by Eng/Research/Legal
Priority scoring rubric implemented as a spreadsheet + exportable JSON
Diligence template (prompt sets, latency/quality thresholds, procurement checklist) approved by PM and Legal
Pilot decision for 12 flavors with recommended rollout plan (canary cohorts, fallback variants) delivered
tasks: PM: define initial signal taxonomy and weight candidates (Aisha)
Research: run 3 representative benchmarks (latency, cost, quality) across us-east/us-west/apac (TBD)
Eng: validate quant-compatibility and estimate infra delta for 3 high-priority flavors (ENG-5421)
Legal: quick-licensing triage on top-5 risky suppliers
Analytics: create prioritization sheet and automated ingest from telemetry (events + usage patterns)
Console: add tag taxonomy for 'shelf-candidate' and 'shelf-deprecate'

research_findings_summary: Preliminary bench notes: (1) Several small-context open models show parity on intent classification but differ 2-3x in token throughput when quantized; (2) One vendor has region-limited availability causing a measurable tail in 99th pctl latency; (3) Embedding vector norms are consistent across 3 flavors we tested, but index recall degrades on lower-dimension quant variants; implication: prioritize quant-compatibility and regional redundancy as first-order signals.
decision: Pilot approval (provisional): run canary onboarding for 2 medium-priority flavors (one quant-friendly, one high-accuracy single-precision) to validate infra cost and quality delta. If 99th pctl latency remains within SLO and quality drop <2% on our eval set, proceed to broader shelf onboarding. Otherwise, trigger fallbacks and re-evaluate weights.
